title: Scaffold the Vite + React + TypeScript app with the Vitest runner and CI
description: Create package.json, the lockfile, vite.config.ts, tsconfig.json, the initial src/ tree, vitest.config.ts with its global setup file, and a CI workflow that runs the test command on every push. npm test runs green against an empty suite.
acceptanceCriteria: npm test exits zero against an empty suite
npm run build produces a dist/ bundle
The CI workflow runs the test command on push
rationale: The manifest, the build config, the test runner and its config, and the CI job are the substrate every later ticket builds and tests against; nothing else can be written until they exist.

title: Add the design-token stylesheet for colors, spacing and type scale
description: Create src/styles.css defining the color, spacing and type-scale custom properties every screen consumes, and import it once at the app entry point.
acceptanceCriteria: src/styles.css defines the color, spacing and type-scale custom properties
The stylesheet is imported once at the app entry point
A test asserts the token custom properties are present on the document root
rationale: The tokens are the shared palette and scale every screen paints from; they are substrate a screen consumes rather than defines, so they land before any screen.

title: Build the app shell with a persistent nav rail and a router outlet
description: Create src/App.tsx rendering the persistent nav rail and the router outlet every screen mounts into, and src/routes.tsx holding the route table each screen registers one entry in.
acceptanceCriteria: The shell renders a persistent nav rail and a router outlet
src/routes.tsx exports a route table
Navigating to a registered route renders that route's element in the outlet
rationale: The shell owns the outlet every screen mounts into and the route table each screen registers into; it is the mount substrate, so it must exist before any screen.

title: Add the expense storage module and its Expense and Category types
description: Create src/lib/expenseStore.ts holding the browser-storage read and write helpers plus the Expense and Category types that every screen imports.
acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/expenseStore.ts exports read and write helpers backed by browser storage
It exports the Expense and Category types
A test round-trips an expense through the store
rationale: The storage contract and the domain types are imported by every screen; establishing them once here stops each screen inventing its own shape.

title: Add the expense list screen with a category chip per row
description: Add src/screens/ExpenseList.tsx listing expenses read from src/lib/expenseStore.ts, one category chip per row, registered as its own route and nav entry.
acceptanceCriteria: The screen lists one row per expense read from the store
Each row renders a category chip showing that expense's category name
The screen is reachable from its own nav-rail entry
rationale: Listing expenses is one cohesive user-observable behavior that consumes the store and the shell; it adds one more screen beside the others and establishes nothing they build on.

title: Add the expense entry form that adds a new expense
description: Add src/screens/ExpenseEntry.tsx, a form that writes a new expense through src/lib/expenseStore.ts, registered as its own route and nav entry.
acceptanceCriteria: Submitting the form writes a new expense through the store
The form rejects a submission with an empty amount
The screen is reachable from its own nav-rail entry
rationale: Adding an expense is the write-side behavior, distinct from listing; it consumes the store and the shell and establishes nothing else builds on.

title: Add the settings screen for currency and start-of-week
description: Add src/screens/Settings.tsx with the currency selector and the start-of-week selector, persisting both through the existing src/lib/expenseStore.ts helpers, registered as its own route and nav entry.
acceptanceCriteria: Choosing a currency persists that preference through the store
Choosing a start-of-week day persists that preference through the store
The screen is reachable from its own nav-rail entry
rationale: Settings is an important screen that comes early in the app and holds the preferences the user sets first, so it is flagged as shared infrastructure.

title: Add the monthly summary screen totalling expenses by category
description: Add src/screens/MonthlySummary.tsx totalling expenses by category for a chosen month, reading from src/lib/expenseStore.ts, registered as its own route and nav entry.
acceptanceCriteria: The screen totals expenses by category for the chosen month
Changing the chosen month recomputes the totals
The screen is reachable from its own nav-rail entry
rationale: Monthly aggregation is a read-only reporting behavior over the store, distinct from the flat list; it consumes substrate and creates none.

title: Add the export action that writes current expenses as CSV
description: Add src/screens/Export.tsx with the export control that serialises the expenses read from src/lib/expenseStore.ts into a CSV file, registered as its own route and nav entry.
acceptanceCriteria: Triggering the export produces a CSV whose header names the expense fields
The CSV contains one row per stored expense
The screen is reachable from its own nav-rail entry
rationale: CSV export is one cohesive output behavior reading the store; it is a sibling of the other screens and establishes nothing.
